plan.rationale: The goal is disclosed from step one, so the only branch that ever needs to drive is the goal-seeking one; `toy_avoid_obstacles` is chosen over `toy_drive_to_goal` because in an unmapped indoor space with occluding walls the route is not a straight line and a pure bearing/range reducer would drive into furniture, whereas this node reduces range while keeping clear. `toy_is_goal_known` is ticked first to write the `goal_known` Flag that both actions read, and `toy_sweep_for_goal` sits last in the fallback purely as a recovery leg for the (here impossible) case of an undisclosed goal, since its precondition is the exact complement of the avoider's. `gen_b_d6ae93648c7b4f25` is omitted deliberately: it only publishes a `Speed` on an out port, and no node in the available set declares a `Speed` in port, so there is no channel through which its braking-distance limit could reach the driving action — sequencing it would starve one of the two rather than combine them.
